SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the morning, your shadow falls towards which direction? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. West
   C. Nowhere
   D. East

2. Which country lies to the south of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Ethiopia
   B. South Sudan
   C. Uganda
   D. Tanzania

3. What is the best way to compare the sizes of two counties on maps? (1 mark)
   A. Compare the length of the names
   B. Use the same scale and compare the areas
   C. Guess without a map
   D. Count the number of towns only

4. On a physical map, what colour is used for water? (1 mark)
   A. Brown
   B. Red
   C. Black
   D. Blue

5. What is a lake? (1 mark)
   A. A large area of water surrounded by land
   B. A dry plain
   C. A long channel of flowing water
   D. A very high mountain

6. During the dry season herders in dry areas often do what? (1 mark)
   A. Collect rainwater
   B. Sell umbrellas
   C. Plant maize
   D. Move animals to find water and grass

7. What should you do when visiting a museum? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   B. Shout loudly
   C. Run around the halls
   D. Take objects home

8. Fort Jesus is found in which town? (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru
   B. Kisumu
   C. Eldoret
   D. Mombasa

9. Why do tourists visit historic places? (1 mark)
   A. To plant maize
   B. To cut trees
   C. To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
   D. To buy soap

10. Gede Ruins are near which coastal town? (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru
   B. Kisumu
   C. Watamu
   D. Nyeri

11. Why do herders in dry areas not live crowded in one place? (1 mark)
   A. They have no families
   B. They do not use water
   C. They move with animals to look for water and grass
   D. They dislike roads

12. In a shaded map, which shade usually shows the most crowded area? (1 mark)
   A. No shade
   B. White
   C. The lightest shade
   D. The darkest shade

13. On a dot map, what does a group of many dots close together show? (1 mark)
   A. A crowded area
   B. A road
   C. A river
   D. An empty area

14. Which of these is a traditional drink of the Kalenjin? (1 mark)
   A. Coffee
   B. Cola
   C. Mursik
   D. Wine

15. Where is soda ash taken from in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Victoria
   B. Kisumu Port
   C. Lake Magadi
   D. Mount Kenya

16. Which of these is a safe way for a child to take part in economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. Helping in the school garden
   B. Working at night
   C. Working in a quarry
   D. Carrying heavy loads all day

17. What is the raw material for tea? (1 mark)
   A. Tea leaves
   B. Cotton
   C. Fish
   D. Sugarcane

18. What is an industry? (1 mark)
   A. A type of weather
   B. A school subject
   C. A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   D. A kind of farm animal

19. Which town is Kenya's main port and a busy industrial town? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Kericho
   C. Nyeri
   D. Mombasa

20. Which of these is a way of living in peace with others? (1 mark)
   A. Teasing
   B. Sharing what you have
   C. Cheating
   D. Grabbing things

21. What should you do if someone makes you feel unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   B. Stay silent
   C. Fight
   D. Keep it a secret

22. What is child trafficking? (1 mark)
   A. Taking children on a picnic
   B. Adopting children legally
   C. Taking children to school
   D. Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them

23. How many tally marks does a group of five look like? (1 mark)
   A. Four lines crossed by one line
   B. Two lines
   C. Six lines
   D. One line

24. What is an election? (1 mark)
   A. A school holiday
   B. A prayer
   C. A kind of game
   D. A process where people vote to choose leaders

25. Who takes over when the president of the Children's Government is absent? (1 mark)
   A. The cook
   B. The deputy president
   C. The visitor
   D. The parent

26. Which quality means telling the truth? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Honesty
   C. Pride
   D. Laziness

27. What do village elders do? (1 mark)
   A. Teach maths only
   B. Make cars
   C. Welcome visitors and help settle small quarrels
   D. Fly aeroplanes

28. What is a community? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. A school subject
   C. A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   D. A kind of animal

29. Why is it important for leaders to have good qualities? (1 mark)
   A. People fear them
   B. People trust them and live in peace
   C. People quarrel
   D. Resources are wasted

30. Who elects the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The teachers
   B. The president alone
   C. Registered voters in the county
   D. The chief

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Match each activity to a resource it uses: fishing, farming, mining, tourism. (4 marks)

32. Write a short motto for a school and say what it means. (3 marks)

33. Name two duties of a pupil in school. (2 marks)

34. Explain what neighbouring counties are. (2 marks)

35. Explain why children must not be forced to do hard work. (3 marks)

36. Describe three ways in which pupils can take part in conserving a historic place near their school. (3 marks)

37. What is a sub-county? (2 marks)

38. Who is the patron of a Children's Government? (2 marks)

39. Write a short motto and explain what it asks pupils to do. (3 marks)

40. Explain the meaning of an economic activity and give two examples. (3 marks)

41. Describe the duties of ward and village administrators. (4 marks)

42. State two things a good map key should show. (2 marks)

43. Describe how to interview an elder about traditional culture politely. (4 marks)

44. Give two examples of goods and two examples of services. (4 marks)

45. Why should you never shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm? (2 marks)

46. Explain how a historic place such as Fort Jesus helps local people to earn a living. (4 marks)

47. Give three ways in which the dry season affects people's activities. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — West
   The sun is in the east in the morning, so shadows point west.

2. D — Tanzania
   Tanzania borders Kenya to the south.

3. B — Use the same scale and compare the areas
   To compare fairly we use maps drawn to the same scale.

4. D — Blue
   Blue is used for lakes, rivers and the ocean.

5. A — A large area of water surrounded by land
   A lake has land all around it.

6. D — Move animals to find water and grass
   Grass and water become scarce, so herders move.

7. A — Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   Good manners protect the objects and other visitors.

8. D — Mombasa
   Fort Jesus is a fort at Mombasa.

9. C — To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
   Tourism brings income to the local people.

10. C — Watamu
   Gede Ruins are near Watamu in Kilifi County.

11. C — They move with animals to look for water and grass
   Herding needs large areas of pasture.

12. D — The darkest shade
   Dark shades show higher numbers.

13. A — A crowded area
   Many dots show many people.

14. C — Mursik
   Mursik is fermented milk.

15. C — Lake Magadi
   Soda ash is mined at Lake Magadi.

16. A — Helping in the school garden
   Light safe work under supervision is fine.

17. A — Tea leaves
   Tea is made from tea leaves.

18. C — A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   Industries change raw materials into products or provide services.

19. D — Mombasa
   Mombasa is Kenya's main port.

20. B — Sharing what you have
   Sharing shows kindness.

21. A — Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   Telling an adult is right.

22. D — Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   Trafficking is a crime.

23. A — Four lines crossed by one line
   A group of five has four vertical lines and one crossing them.

24. D — A process where people vote to choose leaders
   Elections choose leaders.

25. B — The deputy president
   The deputy helps and takes over.

26. B — Honesty
   Honesty is truthfulness.

27. C — Welcome visitors and help settle small quarrels
   Village elders help the village.

28. C — A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   People in a community share a market, a school or customs.

29. B — People trust them and live in peace
   Good leaders build trust and peace.

30. C — Registered voters in the county
   Voters in the county elect the governor.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fishing uses lakes or ocean, farming uses land and soil, mining uses minerals, tourism uses wildlife or beaches.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It means pupils should study well and be kind to others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for its meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Follow the school rules and respect others. Accept care for property or do class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neighbouring counties are counties that share a boundary with your county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing a boundary, 1 mark for saying they are next to yours.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: It harms their health, it stops them going to school, and it is child labour, which is against the law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweep and pick up litter, report damage to an adult, and tell others why the place is important.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sub-county is a smaller part of a county. Each county is divided into sub-counties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it is a smaller part, 1 mark for the link with a county.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: The patron is a teacher who guides and advises the pupil leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a teacher, 1 mark for guides the pupil leaders.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It asks pupils to study well and treat others with kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: An economic activity is work done to earn income or produce goods and services. Examples are farming and fishing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: They bring county services close to people, pass on information, help organise public meetings, and take the community's needs to county leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The meaning of the colours and the meaning of the lines or symbols used on the map.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet the elder respectfully, ask permission before recording or taking photographs, listen without interrupting, and say thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Goods: maize and shoes. Services: teaching and nursing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lightning can strike tall trees. It is safer to go into a strong building.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 1 mark for a safer choice.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Visitors pay entry fees, guides are employed, hotels and restaurants get customers, and craft sellers sell to tourists.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Farmers harvest and dry crops, fishermen dry fish in the sun, and herders move animals to find water and grass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.
